newsitem.title: USA: NY Senate again passes utility legislation package.
newsitem.headline: NY Senate again passes utility legislation package.

text.p: The New York State Senate has again passed three pieces of legislation backers expect will significantly reduce electric utility rates.
The package does not have a sponsor in the Assembly, according to Charles Carrier, a spokesman for Speaker Sheldon Silver.

Noting "parts of New York have the highest energy costs in the country," Senate Majority Leader Joseph L. Bruno said: "The bills we passed (Wednesday) will reduce those costs and guarantee that savings will be passed along to ratepayers in the form of lower monthly utility bills."

A spokesman for the majority said Friday the "only significant change" in the legislative package from the version passed by the Senate last year is "minor changes to assure (resulting) savings go to rate payers."
The Senate passed a bill that would phase-out the Gross Receipts Tax on energy and telecommunications. It would freeze the tax in 1997, then phase it out over the next four years.
A statement released by the Senate majority said phasing-out the GRT would save ratepayers $710 million a year when fully implemented.
The statement included the following utility-by-utility estimate of the portion of each revenue dollar going to taxes, saying it was provided by the Energy Association of New York.
Electric Utility State Local State & Local

It said the Senate approved the "Electric Ratepayer Relief Act", also known as the "Securitization" bill, which would establish a financing mechanism for the state's electric utilities to obtain lower cost financing which will result in lower electric rates.

Also passed was the "Power For Prosperity" bill designed to make 400 megawatts of low cost power available for economic development. The power, provided jointly by the state Power Authority and investor-owned utilities, would be made available to businesses for the purpose of job retention.
